sections.title: Referral
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Write a formal paragraph summarizing the referral and assessment process for a mental health report. Use the following details:

Referring professional’s name

Full address of the referring clinic

Referral date

Reason for referral

Date of assessment

Format of the session (in person, video, phone)

Duration of clinical interview

Tools used (e.g., BDI-II, BAI, PCL)

Time allocated for scoring and report preparation

Whether the client was informed about the purpose of the assessment

Whether confidentiality and report content were explained

Whether the client was encouraged to ask questions

Whether any conflicts of interest were identified
Use a professional clinical tone and refer to the client by last name only.

Example Output:
Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] was referred for psychotherapy by [Referring Professional’s Full Name] of [Clinic Name], located at [Clinic Full Address]. The referral, dated [Referral Date], was made to address symptoms related to [Reason for Referral]. A mental health assessment was conducted on [Assessment Date] via [Session Format]. The process included a [Duration of Clinical Interview] clinical interview and the use of standardized self-report tools, including [Selected Tools: e.g., Beck Depression Inventory–II (BDI-II), Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), PTSD Checklist (PCL)]. An additional [Time Used for Scoring and Report] was allocated for scoring and preparing the final report.

Prior to the assessment, Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] was informed about the purpose of the evaluation, the intended use of the findings to support psychotherapy services, and the limits of confidentiality. He/She/They confirmed understanding and was encouraged to ask questions throughout the process. [Conflict of Interest Identified or Not].

questions.questionText: What is the name of the referring professional?
What is the full address of the referring professional or clinic?
What is the referral date?
What is the stated reason for referral?

sections.title: Inform Consent
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Prompt:

Write a formal paragraph summarizing the informed consent process during a mental health assessment. The paragraph should address the following elements:

Whether the client was informed about the purpose of the assessment

Whether the client was informed about the limits of confidentiality

Whether the client was informed that the assessment report would include personal and clinical information, a treatment plan, and recommendations

Whether the client was encouraged to ask questions prior to signing the consent form

Whether the client was informed that the report would be submitted to their insurance provider, if applicable

Whether the purpose of the submission (e.g., to support pre-approval for psychotherapy services) was clearly explained

Use a clinical and professional tone. Refer to the client only by last name, using appropriate honorifics (Mr./Ms.) and pronouns.

Example Output (with placeholders):

During the assessment session, Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] was informed of the purpose of the mental health assessment and the limits of confidentiality. He/She/They was advised that the resulting report would include personal and clinical information, the assessor’s clinical impressions, a recommended treatment plan, and relevant recommendations. Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] was encouraged to ask questions regarding the assessment process and the release of information prior to signing the informed consent form. He/She/They was also informed that the completed report would be submitted to their insurance provider, where applicable, for the purpose of supporting pre-approval for psychotherapy services.

questions.questionText: Was the client informed about the purpose of the mental health assessment?
Was the client informed about the limits of confidentiality, including legal and ethical exceptions?
Was the client informed that the assessment report would include personal and clinical information?
Was the client encouraged to ask questions about the assessment process and the release of information prior to signing the consent form?
Was the client informed that the completed report may be submitted to their insurance provider?
Was the purpose of submitting the report (e.g., to support pre-approval for psychotherapy services) explained to the client?
Did the client provide informed consent after receiving the above explanations?

sections.title: Sources of Information
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Prompt:
Write a formal paragraph summarizing the sources of information used in a mental health assessment. Include the following inputs:

Whether a semi-structured clinical interview was conducted

Whether the interview explored current and historical mental health functioning

Whether the client's social background was reviewed

Whether behavioral observations were made

Whether psychological testing was administered

The specific tools used (e.g., BDI-II, BAI, PCL)
Use a professional clinical tone and refer to the client only by last name.

🔹 Example Output (with Placeholders)
The information included in this report was derived from multiple sources. A semi-structured clinical interview was conducted to explore Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name]’s current and historical mental health functioning, as well as relevant aspects of [his/her/their] social background. The interview process also allowed for pertinent behavioral observations to be made.

Psychological testing was administered, and the assessment battery included [List of Tools Used, e.g., Beck Depression Inventory–II (BDI-II), Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), PTSD Checklist (PCL)].

questions.questionText: Was a semi-structured clinical interview conducted as part of this assessment?
Did the clinical interview explore current and historical mental health functioning?
Were behavioral observations made during the assessment process?
Was self-reported assessment tools  administered as part of this assessment?
Which self-reported assessment tools tools were administered?

sections.title: Behavioral Observations
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Prompt:

Write a formal clinical paragraph describing the client’s attendance, engagement, and behavioral presentation during a mental health assessment session.

The paragraph should include:

Whether the session was conducted in person at the clinic

The client’s willingness to share personal history, experiences, and challenges

The client’s punctuality and level of engagement throughout the session

Observations of the client’s attitude and level of cooperation

The quality of communication and rapport established with the clinician

Observations related to tone of voice and speech rate

The client’s emotional presentation at the beginning of the session (e.g., signs of anxiety)

The client’s expressed motivation or willingness to work on identified issues and develop coping strategies

Use a professional and objective clinical tone. Refer to the client only by last name. Do not include diagnostic conclusions or treatment recommendations.

questions.questionText: What was the format of the assessment session?
How did the client attend and engage during the session?

options.optionText: Demonstrated willingness to share personal history, experiences, and challenges

options.optionText: Communicated effectively and established positive rapport

sections.title: Risk Factors
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Prompt:

Write a formal clinical paragraph summarizing the client’s risk assessment and safety planning discussed during the mental health assessment.

The paragraph should include:

Whether the client denied current suicidal ideation

Whether the client denied suicidal intent or a plan

Whether the client denied current thoughts of self-harm

Whether safety planning was discussed

Whether the client agreed to seek support if suicidal thoughts emerge

Whether the client agreed to present to emergency services if suicidal intent or a plan develops

Use a professional and objective clinical tone. Refer to the client only by last name. Do not include diagnostic conclusions, speculation, or graphic detail.

questions.questionText: Did the client report any current suicidal thoughts?
Did the client report any current suicidal intent?
Did the client report having a current suicidal plan?
Did the client report any current thoughts of self-harm?

sections.title: Relevant Background Information
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Prompt:

Write a formal, well-organized paragraph summarizing the client’s relevant background information based solely on the details provided during the assessment.

When writing the paragraph:

Maintain a client-focused and objective clinical tone

Refer to the client only by last name

Use attribution language such as “the client reported,” “the client stated,” or “the client expressed” to clearly indicate self-reported information

Preserve all details exactly as provided, without adding, removing, or interpreting information

Do not reduce, summarize, or generalize the content

Improve clarity, organization, and flow while keeping the original meaning intact

Avoid diagnostic language, assumptions, or clinical conclusions

The goal is to organize and present the information clearly and professionally, while accurately reflecting the client’s reported experiences.

questions.questionText: Can you provide details about your medical history, including any current or past medical conditions, hospitalizations, medications you have taken or are currently taking, and any previous medical diagnoses?
Can you provide information about your developmental history, including early childhood development, learning experiences, and any developmental concerns that were identified while growing up?
Can you describe your emotional history, including past or current emotional difficulties, ongoing fears, mood changes, or significant life events that have impacted your emotional well-being?
Are there any additional emotional aspects or experiences that you feel are important to mention?

sections.title: Presenting Concerns
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Prompt:
Write a formal, narrative-style paragraph for the Presenting Concerns section of a mental health assessment report. Use the following client-reported data:

Physical concerns selected (e.g., sleep disturbances, fatigue, pain, etc.)

Emotional concerns selected (e.g., sadness, anxiety, panic attacks, irritability, etc.)

Social and relational concerns selected (e.g., social withdrawal, isolation, family conflict, etc.)

Cognitive or thinking-related concerns selected (e.g., trouble concentrating, intrusive thoughts, memory difficulties, etc.)

Only include the items actually reported. Do not assume or generalize. Use a clinical and objective tone, refer to the client by last name only, and write in third person. Clearly describe how the reported symptoms affect functioning or emotional well-being.
Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] presented with a range of physical and psychological concerns reported over the past month. Physically, [he/she/they] endorsed experiencing [insert selected physical concerns, e.g., trouble sleeping, chronic fatigue, and muscle tension], which have contributed to difficulties maintaining daily routines and energy levels.

Emotionally, [Client Last Name] reported experiencing [insert selected emotional concerns, e.g., persistent sadness, anxiety, and episodes of panic], often accompanied by feelings of helplessness or internal tension.

Socially, [he/she/they] indicated [insert selected social/relational concerns, e.g., increased social withdrawal and a sense of isolation], particularly following migration-related losses. These changes have reportedly disrupted [his/her/their] ability to maintain supportive relationships.

Cognitively, [Client Last Name] described [insert selected cognitive concerns, e.g., trouble focusing and frequent intrusive thoughts], which interfere with concentration and emotional regulation. Together, these symptoms appear to reflect ongoing distress and challenges in adapting to current life circumstances.

sections.title: Beck Depression Inventory
sections.description: Instructions: This questionnaire consists of 21 groups of statements. Please read each group carefully and select the one statement that best describes how you have been feeling during the past two weeks, including today. Circle the number beside the selected statement. If more than one statement in a group seems to apply, choose the one with the highest number. Make sure to select only one statement per group, including for item 16 (Changes in Sleeping Pattern) and item 18 (Changes in Appetite).
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Prompt:
Write the results section for the Beck Depression Inventory–II (BDI-II) as part of a mental health assessment report. Use a formal and objective clinical tone consistent with professional mental health documentation. Refer to the client only by last name.

Include the following details:

Client’s last name

Total BDI-II score

Severity classification, based on total score:

0–13 = Minimal

14–19 = Mild

20–28 = Moderate

29–63 = Severe

Symptoms endorsed at each severity level:

Score of 3 = Severe

Score of 2 = Moderate

Score of 1 = Mild

Score of 0 = Not endorsed

Whether suicidal thoughts were endorsed and their severity

Whether suicidal ideation, intent, or plan is currently present

Whether the client demonstrated insight and willingness to seek support

Example Output (with Placeholders)
Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] was administered the Beck Depression Inventory–II (BDI-II), a 21-item standardized self-report measure designed to assess the severity of depressive symptoms over the two weeks preceding the assessment. [He/She/They] obtained a total score of [Total Score], which falls within the [Severity Category] range of depressive symptomatology.

Severe symptoms (score of 3) were endorsed in the areas of [list]. Moderate symptoms (score of 2) were reported in relation to [list]. Mild symptoms (score of 1) were reported in [list], while no symptoms (score of 0) were noted in [list].

Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] [did/did not] endorse suicidal thoughts, rated at a severity of [score]. [He/She/They] denied any current suicidal ideation, intent, or plan. [He/She/They] demonstrated insight into their mental health and expressed a willingness to seek support if symptoms were to worsen or safety concerns were to arise.

sections.title: Beck Anxiety Inventory
sections.description:
Please read each of the following statements carefully. The list describes common symptoms of anxiety. For each item, select the number that best reflects how much you have been bothered by that symptom during the past month, including today.

Use the following scale to rate each symptom:

0 – Not at all

1 – Mildly (it didn’t bother me much)

2 – Moderately (it wasn’t pleasant at times)

3 – Severely (it bothered me a lot)

Simply click or select the number that matches your experience for each item.
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Prompt:
Write the results section for the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI) as part of a mental health assessment report. Use a professional, objective tone consistent with mental health documentation. Refer to the client only by last name.

Include the following elements:

Client’s last name

Total BAI score

Severity classification based on score:

0–7 = Minimal

8–15 = Mild

16–25 = Moderate

26–63 = Severe

Symptoms rated as:

Score of 3 = Severe

Score of 2 = Moderate

Score of 1 = Mild

Score of 0 = Not endorsed

Whether symptoms are primarily physiological (somatic), cognitive, or a mix of both

Whether panic attacks were reported

Whether the client demonstrated emotional insight and willingness to engage in treatment
 Example Output (with Placeholders)
Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] was administered the Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI), a 21-item standardized self-report instrument used to assess the severity of anxiety symptoms experienced during the week preceding the assessment. [He/She/They] obtained a total score of [Total Score], which falls within the [Severity Category] range of anxiety symptomatology.

Severe symptoms (score of 3) were reported across the following areas: [list]. A moderate symptom (score of 2) was reported in [list], while mild symptoms (score of 1) were endorsed in [list]. Items rated with a score of 0 (not endorsed) included [list].

The overall symptom pattern reflects [a primarily physiological profile / primarily cognitive symptoms / a combination of cognitive and somatic symptoms], marked by [brief summary, e.g., intense physiological arousal, persistent fear-based cognition, etc.]. Although panic attacks were [reported / not reported], the breadth and severity of symptoms suggest a substantial impact on daily functioning. Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] demonstrated awareness of [his/her/their] mental health challenges and expressed openness to pursuing therapeutic support.

sections.title: PTSD Checklist (PCL)
sections.description:
The following is a list of problems and concerns that individuals may experience in response to stressful life events. Please read each statement carefully and select the option that best describes how much you have been bothered by that problem during the past month, including today.

Use the following scale to indicate your response:

Not at all (1)

A little bit (2)

Moderately (3)

Quite a bit (4)

Extremely (5)

Please answer every item by selecting one response per question.
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Prompt:
Write the results section for the PTSD Checklist (PCL) as part of a mental health assessment report. Use a clinical, objective tone consistent with formal mental health documentation. Refer to the client only by last name.

Include the following elements:

Client’s last name

Total PCL score

Whether the score exceeds the clinical threshold for PTSD

Items rated:

Score of 5 = Severe

Score of 4 = Moderate

Score of 3 or below = Mild or not clinically significant

Specific symptoms endorsed (e.g., intrusive memories, flashbacks, avoidance, emotional numbing, hypervigilance, sleep disturbance, concentration difficulties)

Whether the symptom pattern includes re-experiencing, avoidance, emotional detachment, and/or arousal

Brief conclusion about the impact on functioning and the need for trauma-informed care
Example Output (with Placeholders)
Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] completed the PTSD Checklist (PCL), a 17-item standardized self-report measure designed to assess symptoms of post-traumatic stress over the past month, based on DSM-IV criteria. [He/She/They] obtained a total score of [Total Score], which [does/does not] exceed the clinical threshold and is indicative of [significant/minimal] post-traumatic stress symptomatology.

Mr./Ms. [Client Last Name] endorsed the highest level of severity (score of 5) across the following domains: [list of symptoms]. A moderate symptom (score of 4) was reported for [list], while a mild symptom (score of 1–3) was noted in [list].

The overall pattern reflects a trauma response characterized by [re-experiencing/intrusions], [avoidance of trauma-related cues], [emotional numbing or detachment], and [hyperarousal or vigilance]. This profile suggests persistent psychological distress with a substantial impact on daily functioning. These findings support the need for focused, trauma-informed intervention to address the underlying emotional and cognitive consequences of past trauma.

sections.title: Assessment Summary
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Generate a concise Assessment Summary written in a client-centered, professional tone for inclusion in a psychological or mental health assessment report.

The summary must not exceed two paragraphs and must be written in a clear narrative (paragraph) style, not in bullet points or headings.

The content of the summary must be based exclusively on information already documented in the Presenting Concerns section.
Do not introduce new symptoms, background details, interpretations, assumptions, or examples that are not explicitly stated in that section.

The first paragraph must begin by identifying who referred the client and the reason for referral, using only wording and details already present in the Presenting Concerns section.

The second paragraph must summarize the client’s reported experiences and difficulties, using language that closely reflects how the client expressed their concerns in the Presenting Concerns section. Symptoms should be integrated naturally within the paragraph and may reflect emotional, cognitive, behavioral, physical, or functional experiences only if these are already described.

Use neutral, respectful, and non-diagnostic language, with phrasing such as “the client reports,” “the client describes,” or “the client indicates experiencing.”

Emphasize the impact of the reported concerns on daily functioning and overall well-being, only as described by the client.

Do not add clinical interpretation, diagnostic conclusions, severity ratings, timelines, or treatment recommendations.

The final output should read as a polished, professional narrative suitable for formal documentation.

questions.questionText: Would you like to include the Assessment Summary?

sections.title: Treatment Plan
sections.aiReportPrompt:
Generate 4–5 treatment goals based exclusively on the Presenting Symptoms section of the report.

Each treatment goal must be directly aligned with symptoms explicitly reported by the client.
Do not introduce new concerns, symptoms, needs, or assumptions beyond what is documented in the Presenting Symptoms section.

Write the goals in a client-centered, professional tone, focusing on improving the client’s functioning, coping, emotional regulation, or overall well-being as described by the client.

For each goal, include a brief statement (one short phrase or sentence) describing the method(s) of achieving the goal (e.g., psychoeducation, skill development, supportive exploration, coping strategies), without naming specific therapeutic models unless already referenced elsewhere in the report.

Goals should be:

Clear and measurable in intent

Symptom-focused rather than diagnosis-focused

Realistic and supportive of the client’s expressed needs

Avoid clinical interpretation, diagnostic language, or long explanations.

Present the goals as a numbered list, with each goal followed by its brief method of achievement.

questions.questionText: Would you like to include the treatment plan?

fields.helpText:
I, {{CLIENT_FULL_NAME}}, hereby request and agree to participate in individual psychotherapy at Resilience Psychotherapy, Counselling, Consultation, and Research Corp.

I understand that psychotherapy involves discussing my problems and difficulties with a psychotherapist who will provide a supportive, empathic environment. The therapist may help me explore my feelings, thought patterns, and ways of interacting to gain greater self-awareness.

The psychotherapist will not provide direct advice or solutions but will help me identify my own decisions and strategies to address my concerns effectively.

I acknowledge that I have been informed of the nature and purpose of psychotherapy and that I understand what participation involves. I recognize that therapy is a collaborative process that requires open communication and mutual respect between myself and {{THERAPIST_FULL_NAME}}. The following statements summarize my understanding of the conditions, expectations, and boundaries of this therapeutic process:

  • I am free to ask questions about treatment at any time.
  • I understand that psychotherapy can be beneficial but that outcomes cannot be guaranteed.
  • I understand that discussing my issues may be emotionally difficult at times.
  • I can withdraw from treatment at any time, and referrals will be offered if I wish to continue therapy elsewhere.
  • Treatment will be provided by {{THERAPIST_FULL_NAME}}.
  • By attending and participating in sessions, I give my consent for psychotherapy services.

All information related to my treatment (verbal or written) will be kept confidential except under the following circumstances:

  • If I indicate that I may be a danger to myself or others.
  • In the case of suspected abuse of a child under 16.
  • If a known sexual perpetrator is in contact with a child under 16.
  • If I report sexual abuse by a healthcare professional.
  • If my records are subpoenaed by a court of law.
  • If my therapist’s records are randomly audited by the College of Registered Psychotherapists of Ontario (CRPO).

To uphold confidentiality, the therapist will not initiate contact with the client outside of scheduled therapy sessions. The client may initiate contact at their discretion; however, it is recommended that such contact not occur in the presence of others.

No information regarding the client’s treatment will be shared with any third party, including healthcare professionals, without the client’s explicit consent. Whenever possible, this consent will be obtained in writing.

The fee is CA$205 plus GST per 50-minute session and is covered by IFHP. Payment will be claimed directly from the insurer. By signing this consent, I authorize Resilience Psychotherapy to contact the insurance provider on my behalf and process necessary documentation for service claims.

I understand that I must provide at least 48 hours’ notice to cancel or change an appointment so that the time can be offered to another client.

If I cancel within 48 hours or miss a scheduled appointment without notice, I will be billed for the session.

The psychotherapy services outlined in this consent form will be provided by {{THERAPIST_FULL_NAME}}, who is a registered psychotherapist with the College of Registered Psychotherapists of Ontario (CRPO). You may contact your therapist for professional matters or follow-up communication related to your treatment.

Your therapist can be reached by email at {{THERAPIST_EMAIL}} or by phone at {{THERAPIST_PHONE}} during regular business hours. Messages will be returned as soon as possible within standard working times.

By signing below, I, {{CLIENT_FULL_NAME}}, confirm that I have read and understood the contents of this consent form. I acknowledge that I have had the opportunity to ask questions about the information provided, and that those questions have been answered to my satisfaction. I voluntarily agree to participate in individual psychotherapy services with {{THERAPIST_FULL_NAME}} under the terms outlined above.

reportTemplates.name: Progress Report
reportTemplates.aiInstructions:
Review all available client information, including:

• Assessment records and uploaded files labeled Assessment or Initial Assessment.
• Treatment planning information contained within assessment documents.
• Session Notes, Progress Notes, Psychotherapy Records, and uploaded files labeled Session or Session Note.
• Psychometric assessments and outcome measures included in the assessment report.
• Supporting clinical documents, if available.

Session Count Instructions

Determine the total number of completed psychotherapy sessions using the following rules:

• Count only completed sessions whose title includes the word "Psychotherapy."
• If the assessment, intake, or initial assessment documentation explicitly states that a psychotherapy session was conducted during the assessment process, count this as one psychotherapy session.
• Do not count the same session twice. Any psychotherapy session conducted as part of the assessment process should be counted only once.
• Exclude assessment sessions that did not include psychotherapy intervention.
• Exclude intake sessions, consultation sessions, administrative contacts, cancelled appointments, no-show appointments, rescheduled appointments, and incomplete sessions.
• Exclude future scheduled sessions that have not yet occurred.
• Report the total number of completed psychotherapy sessions.
• Report the psychotherapy treatment period using the date of the first completed psychotherapy session and the date of the most recent completed psychotherapy session. Do not list individual session dates unless specifically requested.

Progress Evaluation

Use assessment findings, treatment goals, baseline symptom presentation, psychometric results, and planned interventions as the foundation for evaluating treatment progress.

Review all psychotherapy session notes and summarize the client's progress throughout treatment based solely on documented clinical information. Evaluate:

• Changes in symptom severity and frequency.
• Progress toward treatment goals.
• Development and application of coping strategies.
• Improvements in functioning, emotional regulation, insight, and resilience.
• Remaining challenges, barriers, or ongoing clinical concerns.

Report Generation

Generate a comprehensive psychotherapy progress report using the provided report template. Maintain an objective, professional, evidence-based, and clinically focused tone throughout.

• Use complete narrative paragraphs.
• Avoid unsupported assumptions, interpretations, or speculation.
• Base all findings, conclusions, and recommendations on documented clinical evidence.
• Integrate relevant psychometric findings when available.
• Ensure recommendations logically follow treatment outcomes and current clinical needs.

When reporting treatment participation, include a statement similar to:

"The client participated in [X] completed psychotherapy sessions between [first psychotherapy session date] and [most recent psychotherapy session date]. This total excludes assessment-only appointments, administrative contacts, consultations, cancelled appointments, no-show appointments, and future scheduled sessions."

If additional psychotherapy is clinically indicated, provide a clear rationale and recommend an appropriate number of additional sessions based on the client's documented needs, treatment response, remaining therapeutic goals, symptom persistence, and overall level of functioning.
reportTemplates.structureText:
Psychotherapy Progress Report Template and AI Prompt Guide

PurposeThis template is designed to guide AI-generated psychotherapy progress reports while ensuring consistency, clinical accuracy, and sufficient detail for treatment renewal and progress evaluation.

Client Information

Client Name, Date of Birth, Age, Gender, Report Date, Clinician Name and Credentials.

Referral Information

Referral source, referral date, and reason for referral.

Brief Background Summary

Concise summary of relevant psychosocial, medical, mental health, family, settlement, occupational, educational, and social history.

Clinical Presentation

Summary of presenting symptoms, functional impairments, emotional, cognitive, behavioural, and social concerns at the start of treatment.

Assessment Findings and Initial Treatment Goals

Summarize assessment findings, psychometric results, clinical formulation, treatment goals, and planned interventions established during the assessment.

Treatment Summary and Interventions

State the total number of completed psychotherapy sessions, treatment period, major treatment themes, and interventions utilized.

Overall Clinical Progress 

Review session note and write areas of progress reported during the session and ongoing challenges, linking progress directly to treatment goals.

Recommendations and Future Treatment Focus

Clinical rationale for continued treatment, recommended focus areas, number of additional sessions, and monitoring recommendations.
